blocks.title: The repeating motion
blocks.text: A pendulum bob swings back and forth because gravity accelerates it toward the lowest point. If air resistance and pivot friction are neglected, the bob repeatedly trades gravitational potential energy for kinetic energy while total mechanical energy remains constant.

blocks.title: Turning points
blocks.text: At either turning point the bob is momentarily at rest, so its speed and kinetic energy are zero. Its height and gravitational potential energy are greatest there, but gravity has a tangential component that begins accelerating the bob back toward the center.

blocks.title: Lowest point
blocks.text: At the lowest point the bob has minimum gravitational potential energy and maximum speed. Its kinetic energy is greatest, while the tangential component of gravity is zero at that instant; the tension instead helps provide the inward centripetal acceleration.

blocks.title: Energy accounting
blocks.text: For an ideal pendulum, the sum of kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy is constant. Energy is not used up at the bottom: it has changed form. On the upward swing, kinetic energy decreases by the same amount that potential energy increases.

blocks.title: Predicting speed from height
blocks.text: Conservation of energy gives one half m v squared equal to m g times the vertical drop from a turning point. The mass cancels, so two ideal pendulums released from the same height reach the bottom with the same speed even when their bobs have different masses.

blocks.title: Period for small angles
blocks.text: For small release angles, the pendulum period is approximately two pi times the square root of length divided by gravitational acceleration. Increasing the string length increases the period; changing the bob mass does not change this ideal small-angle period.

blocks.title: Real pendulums
blocks.text: Air resistance and friction at the pivot transfer mechanical energy into thermal energy. The swing amplitude then decreases over time, even though energy is still conserved when the pendulum and its surroundings are treated as the full system.

blocks.title: Velocity and acceleration
blocks.text: Velocity describes the rate and direction of position change, whereas acceleration describes the rate and direction of velocity change. An object may have zero velocity at an instant while still having nonzero acceleration, as the pendulum does at a turning point.
